exercises.q: ___ (весь день, acc. sg.) светило солнце.
exercises.prompt: The sun was shining all day long.
exercises.why: **день → день** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in -ь — declines like DLI's автомобиль: A. автомобиль. Ending -ь → -ь.  **весь → весь** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with день). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending — (no ending) → — (no ending).  Declension: sg. день · дня · дню · день · днём · дне; pl. дни · дней · дням · дни · днями · днях.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Они просидели ___ (вся ночь, acc. sg.).
exercises.why: **ночь → ночь** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -ь — declines like DLI's часть: A. часть. Ending -ь → -ь.  **весь → всю** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with ночь). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новая: A. новую. Ending -вся → -ю (the stem changes: вс-).  Declension: sg. ночь · ночи · ночи · ночь · ночью · ночи; pl. ночи · ночей · ночам · ночи · ночами · ночах.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: В ___ (последний день, acc. pl.) много солдат побросали патроны и ружья.
exercises.why: **день → дни** (acc. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural дни; declines like DLI's словари (soft stem): A. словари. Ending -ь → -и, with the fleeting -е- of the stem dropped: дн- + -и.  **последний → последние** (acc. pl., agreeing with дни). Adjective type II, soft — declines like DLI's синие: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending -ие → -ие.  Declension: sg. день · дня · дню · день · днём · дне; pl. дни · дней · дням · дни · днями · днях.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.
